clue.text: Suitable software's apt to involve cost for a start

parts.note: an app is a piece of software; the 's is just the possessive of the surface

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so a letter goes inside the word for apt

parts.note: apt to do something means liable to do it

indicators.note: for a start points to the opening letter of the word cost

explanation.surface: A sales pitch warning that some software tends to bring charges right from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relevant or appropriate to a case is suitable for it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Abroad, mostly in outlying parts of Chile, mobile is functional without O2

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so these letters move into a new order
mostly says the last letter of the word abroad is dropped
the outlying parts of Chile are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A traveller in remote parts of Chile finding their mobile phone works without a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' gives ABROA, and 'outlying parts of' gives CE; 'mobile' rearranges these with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisms that live and work without needing oxygen gas are described this way in biology.

clue.text: Perfect energy food for babies?

parts.note: pure means perfect or unadulterated
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Asking whether the ideal power-giving food for infants exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed, sieved food is typically fed to infants, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Unfortunately Mum I can do almost nil about gas being cut off

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the gas's formula
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled
almost says the last letter of nil is dropped

parts.note: CO is carbon monoxide, a gas

explanation.surface: Someone apologising that Mum can do almost nothing now the gas supply has been disconnected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the shuffled letters wrap around the gas's formula, splitting the rearrangement after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to communicate with anyone, in isolation, is a state of being cut off.

clue.text: Recollect name? As one with this you probably won't

indicators.note: re-collect means gather again, so these letters are gathered into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about remembering a name, observing that with this condition you are unlikely to manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'Recollect name': with this condition you probably won't recall one. 'Recollect' also signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory loss is the condition that stops a sufferer recalling things like names.

clue.text: Hero-worshipper's name appearing in newspaper article?

indicators.note: appearing in says the letter for name sits inside the word for the article

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article

explanation.surface: The name of a celebrity fan turning up in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is the priestess of Greek myth; her lover swam the Hellespont nightly to visit her.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this young man adored the priestess Hero, so he literally worshipped Hero.

clue.text: Somewhat peculiar umbelliferous plant

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A botanist describing a plant of the carrot family as a bit of an oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: The lords-and-ladies or cuckoo-pint belongs to a genus of plants with a hooded flower spike.

clue.text: Right sharp retort about A Pope

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go around the letter A

parts.note: a zinger is a sharp, witty retort

explanation.surface: A cutting reply about a Pope, delivered with precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Ratzinger was the German cardinal elected as Benedict XVI, the Roman Catholic pontiff from 2005 to 2013.

clue.text: Turn up, having first blown fuse

indicators.note: having its first letter blown away, so the word for turn up loses its opening letter

parts.note: to emerge is to turn up or appear

explanation.surface: An electrician arriving after a fuse has blown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuse' looks like the electrical part but is the verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine or join together into one is to fuse, a synonym.

clue.text: Female in a car crash could be Shona

indicators.note: a car crash leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman involved in a road accident, who might be called Shona.
explanation.walkthrough: Shona looks like a woman's first name, but here it is the Bantu people (and language) of Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shona are a people of Zimbabwe, so a Shona person is one example from that continent.

clue.text: Judge is not the first to exclude dangerous dog?

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the word for exclude is dropped

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
a dog that bites is a biter, and a biter is dangerous

explanation.surface: A question of whether a court should ban a vicious dog, the judge not being first to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the B of BAR, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee or adjudicator who settles a dispute is a judge of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Motion perhaps will support reduction of tobacco to a degree

indicators.note: in a down entry, the supporting piece sits below the others
a reduction cuts the last letter off the slang word for tobacco

parts.note: baccy is informal British slang for tobacco
Andrew Motion was the British Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: A parliamentary motion that backs cutting tobacco use to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' looks like a proposal but is the poet Andrew Motion, a Poet Laureate. 'to a degree' looks like 'somewhat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor's degree, and the French school-leaving qualification, both go by this name.

clue.text: Discharge from hospital femur set, fine to go

indicators.note: a broken bone is set, and here the letters are set into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: to go says the letter for fine is removed from the bone's name

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A patient discharged from hospital once a broken thigh bone has been set and is doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' removes F from FEMUR, leaving EMUR; 'set' rearranges H and EMUR. 'Discharge' looks like leaving hospital but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A watery mucus flowing from the nose or eyes is a bodily discharge.

clue.text: Look to introduce tube intravenously? That's tempting

indicators.note: to introduce means to put inside, so the word for look takes the other pieces in

parts.note: to look is to see
a duct is a tube carrying fluid in the body
IV is the medical abbreviation for intravenous(ly)

explanation.surface: A nurse considering putting in a drip, which sounds like an attractive offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring or enticing is tempting, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Men a bit confused with regular disappearances, initially at sea, here?

indicators.note: confused says these letters are mixed up into a new order
initially points to the first letter of the word disappearances

explanation.surface: Some baffled men noticing that things keep vanishing at sea, and asking whether this is the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'here?' leans on the whole clue: the place where things are said to vanish at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of the Atlantic is famous for legends of ships and aircraft vanishing, so it is where such losses happen.

clue.text: Slackening on the job

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a mission is a job or assignment

explanation.surface: Someone easing off while at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An easing or abatement, as of a disease's symptoms, is a slackening.

clue.text: Students won't be stretched by these affordable payments?

definitions.text: Students won't be stretched by these
definitions.meaning: undemanding academic periods would not tax the students taking them
instalment arrangements that are gentle on the purse

explanation.surface: A complaint that undemanding courses let students off lightly, paired with cheap instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle school or university periods are undemanding, and gentle credit conditions are affordable instalments.

clue.text: More than one uniformed official arrives outside embassy warm and dry

indicators.note: outside says the word for arrives goes around the other pieces

parts.note: arrives means comes
a mission is a diplomatic embassy
to air laundry is to warm and dry it

explanation.surface: A uniformed official turning up at an embassy that is pleasantly warm and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformed doormen at hotels and theatres are called by this plural noun, matching more than one official.

clue.text: Queer Street has limits

parts.note: a range is the limits within which something varies

explanation.surface: A road called Queer Street, where boundaries apply; Queer Street is old British slang for being in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense queer means odd or peculiar, a synonym.

clue.text: Acting 18, bats getting duck, not runs

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go crazy and are rearranged
getting one letter and not another says the letter for runs is swapped for the letter for duck

parts.note: the answer to 18 down
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricket report: someone strange batting, out for a duck without scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting duck, not runs' swaps the R of STRANGE for O, giving STOANGE, which 'bats' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing in a theatre means being in front of the audience, so acting fits.

clue.text: Tree twice as small as fir perishes without one

indicators.note: something that perishes breaks down, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
twice says the word as is written two times

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes, followed by the word as taken as written

indicators.note: without says the letter for one is taken out of fir

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tree described as being twice as small as a fir that dies off without a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes I from FIR, leaving FR; 'perishes' shuffles that with ASAS and SAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American species of laurel, whose bark was used for flavouring, is a tree.

clue.text: Dirty mark needs time to shift — it's delicate material

indicators.note: to shift means to move, so the letter for time moves to a new spot in the word

parts.note: a stain is a dirty mark

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: a mark on fine fabric takes time to come out.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth glossy fabric, often silk, is a fine and delicate material.

clue.text: Claim is accurate, just

definitions.meaning: an entitlement, as in a claim to the throne
correct, as in the correct answer

explanation.surface: Someone asserting that a claim is both correct and fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works three ways: an entitlement (noun), correct (adjective), and morally fair (adjective).

clue.text: Mostly sunken object brought up by English diver

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an iceberg is famously mostly under water; berg is short for iceberg

explanation.surface: A diver recovering a sunken wreck from the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' suggests a person in scuba gear, but it is a water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterbird dives underwater to catch fish, so it is a diver.

clue.text: Speaker's to irritate with something hackneyed and old hat

indicators.note: a speaker's version means the word is heard rather than read, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: to try someone's patience is to irritate them
corn is trite, overused sentiment or humour

explanation.surface: A speaker who annoys the audience with clichés that are old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like a phrase for something stale, matching 'hackneyed', but it is a literal antique hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-cornered hat of the eighteenth century is literally an old style of headwear.

clue.text: American dined on original ham

parts.note: dined means ate
ur- is a prefix meaning original or primitive, as in Urtext

explanation.surface: An American who has eaten some fine, authentic ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat but means a poor or inexperienced performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor is an unskilled performer, so ham can mean a non-professional or inept one.

clue.text: Counter-revolutionary avoids opening in Leicester Square

indicators.note: counter means going the opposite way, so the remaining letters are read backwards
avoids says a letter is left out of the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Lenin was the leader of the Russian Revolution

indicators.note: the opening in Leicester is its first letter

explanation.surface: An anti-revolutionary steering clear of a gathering in Leicester Square, the London entertainment district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' drops L from LENIN, leaving ENIN, which 'Counter' turns round. Leicester Square is a famous plaza in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Three multiplied by itself gives this number, so it is a perfect square.

clue.text: Son always seen misbehaving needs special rigour

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A parent saying a boy who is always caught misbehaving needs particular strictness.
explanation.definitionFit: Harshness and strictness are the quality of rigour, a synonym.
